title: Major PM2.5 components promote intracranial aneurysm via TP53: Insights from a comprehensive network analysis.
authors: Li, Guanhui; Yan, Keyu; Sun, Yuxiang; Tian, Longlong; Wang, Shuai; Sun, Guozhu
one_liner_zh: 该文结合网络毒理学与孟德尔随机化研究PM2.5组分经TP53促进颅内动脉瘤，虽含分子对接与动力学模拟，但核心对象为小分子-蛋白互作而非蛋白质-DNA互作，且无TF-DNA结合建模，仅边缘相关。
abstract: In this study, we combined network toxicology with two-sample Mendelian randomization (MR) to investigate the potential mechanisms by which major components of PM2.5 influence the development of intracranial aneurysms (IAs). We first identified the target genes of six representative PM2.5 constituents (lead, cadmium, arsenic, benzo[a]pyrene, formaldehyde, and benzene) using the Comparative Toxicogenomics Database (CTD). We intersected these with a compiled list of intracranial aneurysm-related genes. This analysis highlighted TP53 as a key hub gene. MR analysis revealed a significant causal association between genetically predicted TP53 expression and aneurysm risk, suggesting that higher TP53 levels may be protective against intracranial aneurysm (odds ratio 0.850; 95 % CI: 0.734-0.985; P = 0.030). Subsequent molecular docking and dynamics simulations showed that PM2.5 components-especially benzo[a]pyrene-bind directly to the TP53 protein, potentially interfering with its function. Single-cell RNA sequencing and gene set enrichment analysis further indicated that high TP53 expression may protect vascular integrity and retard aneurysm progression by regulating pathways related to the cell cycle, apoptosis, inflammation, and oxidative stress. Moreover, protein expression and apoptosis assays in our cell-based experiments corroborated our findings. Together, these results form a chain of evidence linking PM2.5 exposure to intracranial aneurysm phenotypes via TP53. Our findings identify TP53 as the core mediator through which PM2.5 constituents promote intracranial aneurysm formation. This study provides new insight into how air pollution induces cerebrovascular disease and suggests potential molecular targets for intracranial aneurysm prevention and intervention.
abstract_zh: 本研究结合网络毒理学与两样本孟德尔随机化（Mendelian randomization, MR）方法，探讨PM2.5主要组分影响颅内动脉瘤（intracranial aneurysms, IAs）发展的潜在机制。我们首先利用比较毒物基因组学数据库（Comparative Toxicogenomics Database, CTD）鉴定了六种代表性PM2.5成分（铅、镉、砷、苯并[a]芘、甲醛和苯）的靶基因，并将其与已整理的颅内动脉瘤相关基因列表进行交集分析。该分析突出显示TP53为关键枢纽基因。MR分析揭示了遗传预测的TP53表达与动脉瘤风险之间存在显著因果关联，提示较高的TP53水平可能对颅内动脉瘤具有保护作用（比值比0.850；95%置信区间：0.734-0.985；P=0.030）。随后的分子对接和动力学模拟显示，PM2.5成分——尤其是苯并[a]芘——直接与TP53蛋白结合，可能干扰其功能。单细胞RNA测序和基因集富集分析进一步表明，高TP53表达可能通过调控与细胞周期、凋亡、炎症和氧化应激相关的通路，保护血管完整性并延缓动脉瘤进展。此外，我们基于细胞的实验中的蛋白表达和凋亡检测结果证实了上述发现。综合来看，这些结果形成了一条证据链，将PM2.5暴露通过TP53与颅内动脉瘤表型联系起来。我们的发现确定TP53为PM2.5成分促进颅内动脉瘤形成的核心介导因子。本研究为空气污染如何诱发脑血管疾病提供了新见解，并为颅内动脉瘤的预防和干预提出了潜在分子靶点。
